tool_input.command: for f in src/features/comments/components/*.tsx src/features/discussions/api/update-discussion.ts src/features/discussions/components/update-discussion.tsx src/testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts; do echo "==== $f"; cat "$f"; done
tool_input.description: Read comment components and update-discussion pattern

result:
The edit feature is in place in `apps/react-vite`: an author can edit their own comments through an Edit button and drawer, and sees a success notification after saving. I didn't run tests, lint, the app, or a type check, and I didn't commit anything.

- **API:** `src/features/comments/api/update-comment.ts` sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` with `{ body }`. Its `useUpdateComment` hook refreshes the comments list and shows a "Comment Updated" notification. That follows the new `features/CLAUDE.md` rule that success notifications live in the `api/` hook.
- **Permission:** `src/lib/authorization.tsx` gets a `comment:update` policy that matches only the comment's author. I didn't reuse `comment:delete` because it also lets admins act on other people's comments, and editing someone else's text shouldn't be allowed.
- **UI:** `src/features/comments/components/update-comment.tsx` is a `FormDrawer` with a body textarea, pre-filled with the current text. `comments-list.tsx` shows it next to Delete, only when the policy passes.
- **Mock API:** `src/testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts` adds a PATCH handler. It requires auth, updates only when the caller is the author, returns 403 otherwise, and writes only `body`.

The existing create and delete flows still call `addNotification` in their components. I left them alone because you didn't ask for that change, but they don't follow the new `api/` rule yet.
